disease_label_per_paper: Chronic active Epstein-Barr virus infection (CAEBV) complicated by pulmonary arterial hypertension in an 11-year-old girl
presentation_summary: 11-year-old girl with 1 month of decreased activity tolerance / dyspnea on exertion and left lower abdominal pain; an outside echocardiogram showed moderate tricuspid regurgitation (velocity 3.56 m/s, estimated PA pressure 50 mm Hg) and symptoms worsened despite 1 month of bosentan.
Admission: T 37.3 C, HR 138/min, RR 24/min, BP 92/61 mm Hg; loud pulmonic second heart sound, non-tender hepatosplenomegaly, eczema-like rash on the left lower limb, no leg edema.

Right heart catheterization: RA pressure 14 mm Hg, PA pressure 81/56/67 mm Hg. Imaging: pulmonary artery dilation, right atrial and right ventricular enlargement with normal RV systolic function, no pulmonary arterial obstruction on CT/perfusion imaging.
Labs: WBC 4.81 x10^9/L, platelets 98 x10^9/L, Hb 120 g/L, CRP 10 mg/L, ESR 29 mm/h, NT-proBNP 96 pg/mL, AST 23 U/L, ALT 36 U/L, total bilirubin 7.7 umol/L, albumin 32.0 g/L, creatinine <29 umol/L.
time_zero_definition: Admission to the referral cardiology department (about 1 month after symptom onset and after 1 month of outside bosentan therapy).

confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: anti-EBV capsid antibody IgG > 750.00 U/mL, early anti-EBV antibody IgG > 150.00 U/mL, and anti-EBV nuclear antibody IgG 315.00 U/mL

confirmatory_findings.finding: Peripheral blood EBV DNA load elevated, including T-cell and NK-cell fractions
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: blood EBV-DNA quantification: 3.33 × 10^4 copies/mL; EBV-TDNA: 2.37 × 10^6 copies/mL; EBV-BDNA: 5.63 × 10^5 copies/mL; and EBV-NK DNA: 6.41 × 10^4 copies/mL

confirmatory_findings.finding: Skin biopsy of left lower limb lesion EBER positive
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Pathological biopsy of the damaged skin on the left lower limb suggested mild proliferation and degeneration of the dermal fibrous tissue, scattered lymphocyte infiltration, and more important result was EBER+
Bone marrow examination showed no signs of hemophagosis.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Exclusion workup negative (rheumatic/immune antibodies, hepatitis viruses, syphilis, CMV, HIV, blood/urine tandem mass spectrometry, whole-exome sequencing)
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: the results of the relevant rheumatic and immune antibodies for this child were negative, as were the results for common pathogens (such as hepatitis viruses, syphilis, CMV, and HIV). Blood urine tandem mass spectrometry was also negative. ... The whole-exome gene test was negative.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Pulmonary vascular resistance index (inconsistent between abstract and case text)
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Case text: calculated pulmonary small-artery resistance (PVRI) of 10.8 Wood; Abstract: pulmonary vascular resistance index (PVRI) of 24 Wood
After considering the pathological results, the following diagnoses were made: CAEBV, PAH (severe, moderate risk), and grade II heart failure.

actual_treatment: acyclovir, bosentan and sildenafil after discharge
conservative chemotherapy at readmission 8 months later

outcome.source_text_value: Eight months later ... EBV spread to multiple systems ... conservative chemotherapy was administered. The patient died 1 month later due to disease progression and gastrointestinal bleeding.

quality_warnings: Presentation is dominated by pulmonary arterial hypertension; the CAEBV diagnosis rests on EBV serology/DNA load and EBER-positive skin biopsy, all kept non-ranking.
PVRI differs between abstract (24 Wood) and case text (10.8 Wood); excluded from ranking.
Creatinine reported only as <29 umol/L (censored); recorded as normal flag.
Outside echocardiogram (before bosentan) and admission echo both reported TR velocity 3.56 m/s; estimated PA systolic pressure 50.7 mm Hg used once.
Readmission 8 months later (CNS, serosal effusions, bone marrow EBER+) is course, not presentation, and is not structured for ranking.
